elements.text: Me and Cheyenne share custody of Holly. She stays here during the week, then it’s weekends with me down in Newfields. Every Sunday night I drive all the way up here and I drop Holly off at Cheyenne’s work.

elements.speaker: PETE
elements.text: Yeah. Anyway, this last time I don’t do that. Cheyenne, she comes all the way down and gets Holly herself.

elements.speaker: PETE
elements.text: She’s tried it before. Showing up Sunday mornings with some lame excuse to steal a half day of daddy- daughter time, you know? But this time she wasn't alone.

elements.speaker: PETE
elements.text: Some fuckin’ douchebag driving a black Chrysler 300. Mass plates. I’d never seen the guy before.
John and Doug share a concerned glance.

elements.speaker: PETE
elements.text: We were scheduled for a court hearing that week. Custody hearing. I was fightin’ for full custody of Holly.

elements.speaker: PETE
elements.text: You kiddin’ me? Her mother’s a dope fiend. Trippin’ balls half the time.

elements.speaker: PETE
elements.text: Shit, man, I swear her and this goon were gonna run off with Holly... My little girl... That was the last time I ever saw her.

elements.speaker: PETE
elements.text: I called you guys. I fucking warned ya’s. But you didn’t listen.
Pete wipes away a tear. He drops his head. He begins to cry.

elements.speaker: PETE
elements.text: My baby girl. It’s her birthday.

elements.speaker: PETE
elements.text: Someone tell me where’s my baby girl?
John and the Captain trade a grim look.
John and Doug exit the precinct and walk across the parking lot. John cradles the box of Mackie’s case files under one arm, his free hand presses the ice pack to his sore jaw.

elements.speaker: DOUG
elements.text: These types of cases, I mean, they can really get to you.
John shoots Doug a “how would you know?” look.

elements.speaker: DOUG
elements.text: How about you join me and Trudy for dinner tonight? It’s good to decompress sometimes, you know?
John smolders, shakes his head in disgust. He takes away the ice pack and tosses it into a trash can.

elements.speaker: JOHN
elements.text: I got a report to write.
They arrive at John’s car. John sets the box of files onto the hood, digs into his pockets for his car keys.

elements.speaker: JOHN
elements.text: You run the plate of that Chrysler?

elements.speaker: DOUG
elements.text: Came back clean. Guy’s a drywall contractor down in Quincy.
John finds his keys, unlocks his car and opens his door.

elements.speaker: JOHN
elements.text: Bullshit. He’s a fucking drug dealer.

elements.speaker: DOUG
elements.text: Maybe. Maybe not. How can I tell that from a plate number?

elements.speaker: JOHN
elements.text: Forget it. I’ll go find out myself.
DOUG          got John. Guy’s a nobody. OK? He’s  take nothing to do with Holly. Just  ya? a damn break for a while, will

elements.speaker: JOHN
elements.text: You gave it your best shot.
John takes offense. He slams his door shut.

elements.speaker: DOUG
elements.text: It’s just... man, it’s like... You’re dad passing away, and like... whatever you and Cheyenne had at one time, it’s--

elements.speaker: DOUG
elements.text: So... in another life Holly could've been your daughter. And I think that’s making you not see things so clearly.

elements.speaker: JOHN
elements.text: Did you listen at all to what Holly’s dad just said in there? And all that El Vaquero bullshit? You got the father and her two best friends telling us things that nobody’s ever heard of before. Except one man.
John digs into the box of files, comes up with a fistful of Mackie’s papers and case photos. He holds them up.
He balls the files up. Tosses them in the air.
Some passing officers stop. They watch John’s outburst.

elements.speaker: JOHN
elements.text: So either you’re too loyal to
Mackie and his lackies to admit that this case stinks, or maybe your just too dumb of a cop to realize it.
Doug is stung. But he takes the high road--

elements.speaker: DOUG
elements.text: I feel sorry for you, John. You know? I really do.
Doug wants to say one more thing... but wisely doesn’t. He turns and heads back into the precinct.
John, instant regret, glances around at all the cop-eyes on him. He opens his car door and throws the box of files in. He then climbs in and slams the door, starts his car and peels away.
A late-autumn snow begins to fall over Dover.
A church organ plays. A choir joins in, singing a hymn, all of it playing over...
Blowing snow. Moored boats sway in the rough waters.

slugline: EXT. NATURE PRESERVE - COUNTRY ROAD - DAY

elements.text: A trail diverts off into the forest. Same trail Holly and her friends travelled a week ago. Pick-up trucks line the roadside. Through the trees, a group of search volunteers in safety vests head toward the trucks. John’s car pulls up.
The volunteers remove their vests. Hope drained from their faces. They glance at John as he walks past them and down the wooded trail.
Church service. The choir sings the hymn to a sparse congregation. Among the choir members is Trudy, hymnal book opened as she sings with conviction, almost a fervor.

slugline: EXT. NATURE PRESERVE - STONE FOUNDATION - DAY

elements.text: Stoney remains of the 1600’s settler’s home where Holly’s hobbyhorse was found. John sits here on the cold foundation, smoking a cigarette, looking out at the snowy forest.
The cabin property and Reggie’s newly-completed patio.
Its foundation made of decorative lattice work. Between gaps in the lattice we catch glimpses of the bulkhead cellar door.
Communion. Trudy in line to receive the Eucharist. She approaches the priest and presents her tongue to him, sensually. The priest lays the wafer on her tongue.
Trudy accepts the body of Christ, looking up at the priest, an odd touch of seduction in her eyes.
The light snaps on showing the cellar. A handyman’s man-cave. Reggie descends the stairs, shirtless, clutching a bottle of scotch. He takes a swig. Not his first of the night.

slugline: INT. SILVER DOLLAR SALOON - BATHROOM - NIGHT

elements.text: The grungy bathroom at the Silver Dollar Saloon. Cheyenne in a cowboy hat studies her strung-out image in the mirror.
She opens her mouth, sticks out her tongue, and places a pill onto it. Ecstacy. She closes her mouth and swallows.
Reggie at a workbench rummaging through a toolbox.
On a shelf are displayed a few photos of Mackie and Reggie -- hunting photos and wartime photos. Best buds, smiling.
Beside him on the bench sits a wicker basket, a small cushion placed inside it. On the cushion sits the bottle of scotch and a large hunting knife.
From the toolbox, Reggie comes up with a disposable needle and a vial of clear liquid -- near empty. He also finds a pill bottle containing pills of various sizes, colors.
He unwraps the needle, sticks its tip into the vial and fills the chamber with the leftover clear liquid.
He carefully sets the needle and pill bottle onto the cushion of the basket alongside the knife and the scotch.
Colorful lights flash across a crowded dance floor. Everyone’s doing the two-step.
Except Cheyenne. She’s rolling like hell on molly, dancing to a beat heard only in her head.
Reggie in just his boxers now. He goes over to a locker and opens it and removes a furry grey costume -- a bunny suit. A very demented-looking bunny suit.
He climbs into the suit. Slips the hideous headpiece on.
He takes the wicker basket and goes over to a heavy steel door and opens it. Only darkness inside.
He steps into the darkness, shuts the door behind him as we see a wood-engraved plaque nailed above the door. It reads:
The snow has stopped. Now a crisp moonlit night.
POV through the windshield as headlights illuminate the dock and the water, and the land on the other side -- State of Maine, no more than a few hundred feet away.
On the car’s dash sits a newly-bought tray of baseballs, emptied of balls. The radio tuned again to sports talk:

elements.speaker: RADIO HOST
elements.text: This isn't Emerson Spencer’s first time drafted. He was picked by Toronto 41st overall out of high school in 2020...
John appears in the headlights. His coat pockets bulge with baseballs. He takes off his coat and hangs it on a dock pier.

elements.speaker: RADIO HOST
elements.text: But he didn't sign, making him the highest unsigned pick from the 2020 Draft...
John begins to warm up, stretches out his arms, shoulders. He takes out a baseball and begins to run through pitch grips.

elements.speaker: RADIO HOST
elements.text: ... Great news for the Red Sox, who now look very keen to invite Spencer to Spring Training.
John throws the ball. In the moonlight we see the ball plop into the harbor. Barely making it halfway across.
SERIES OF SHOTS: John throwing ball after ball, trying to hit the far shoreline, growing more tired after every throw.
One ball left. He backs up. He breaks into a run. At the dock’s edge, he catapults the ball, hard.
He howls. Grabs for his shoulder. The ball soars but falls up short again.
He’s pulled a ligament. He screams out in frustration. At so many things. He tries to walk off the pain. He kicks a trash can in anger.
Trudy and Doug at the dinner table, holding hands, plates of food untouched as Trudy says a blessing of thanks.
John walks in. Bruised cheek and favoring his injured arm. The good arm is carrying a 6-pack of beer.
Doug begins to eat, avoiding John’s eyes. Trudy senses everyone’s sour mood--
John walks away without a word and up to his room. Doug goes on eating. Trudy gets up from the table and goes after John.

slugline: INT. KIERSTEAD HOME - JOHN’S BEDROOM - DAY

elements.text: Young John in his room, dressed in a dark suit, adjusting his tie in the mirror. A knock on the door and Mackie enters, also dressed in funeral attire.

elements.speaker: MACKIE
elements.text: Johnny. Let’s go. We’re gonna be late.
He sizes up his son. Senses the dark mood.

elements.speaker: MACKIE
elements.text: I spoke to Cheyenne’s mom. Cheyenne said she’ll go. She’s gonna be there with you.
John, still trying to get his tie just right, seems a million miles away.
John stops fidgeting with his tie. He stares at himself in the mirror. His hands begin to tremble. His breathing goes hard. Panic sets in.
John claws at his tie, gasping for air.

elements.speaker: YOUNG JOHN
elements.text: No! Oh fuck! No! No, no, no!

elements.speaker: MACKIE
elements.text: Jesus, John, it’s okay. Hey, calm down.
Young John rips off his tie. His legs give out and he almost collapses. He stops himself by clutching the dresser.
Mackie goes over and helps John up. He sits him onto the bed.
John struggles in his father’s arms. Mackie tries to calm him. He squares John’s shoulders, looks him dead in the eye.

elements.speaker: MACKIE
elements.text: John, hey. It’s over. Okay? It’s all over. Look, all we gotta do is go to this funeral, and then everything is behind us. Alright?

elements.speaker: MACKIE
elements.text: You’ll go back to school, then spring training. You’ll feel back to normal in no time. Now trust me.
Mackie moves in for a hug. Young John recoils.

elements.speaker: YOUNG JOHN
elements.text: You think I’m ever gonna play baseball after this?!
Without warning, Mackie’s big powerful hand grabs John’s throat, squeezing.
John struggles, but can’t break free. Mackie’s grip hardens.

elements.speaker: MACKIE
elements.text: This family has done nothing but sacrifice for you! Your poor dead mother. You wanna disappoint her?!
Young Trudy in a black dress stands at the open door. Mackie lets go of Young John. Mackie half turns to his daughter.

elements.speaker: MACKIE
elements.text: Trudy. Get in the car, honey.
Mackie composes himself. He address his son--
He tosses a wad of dollar bills onto the bed.

elements.speaker: MACKIE
elements.text: ... you can take a cab to the
Mackie walks out. Trudy lingers in the doorway, staring in at her older brother sitting on the bed, rubbing his throat. Finally, she turns and walks away.
John sits by the open window, smoking a cigarette. He has a beer in his hand and a cold compress over his shoulder.
Knock on the door. It’s Trudy.

elements.speaker: TRUDY
elements.text: Hey. Sure you don’t want some food?

elements.speaker: TRUDY
elements.text: I see we’re smoking in the house now?
John, not in the mood, flicks the butt out the window. He takes a drink of his beer.

elements.speaker: TRUDY
elements.text: Doug told me what happened at the police station today, with you off the case and--

elements.speaker: JOHN
elements.text: Who gives a shit, Trudy? Seriously.
Trudy, fed up, turns and leaves. She comes back.

elements.speaker: TRUDY
elements.text: You know, Doug is trying his best. Everyone here is just trying their best. So you really didn’t need to go and shit on him like that.
John, sarcastically, shouts down to Doug--
With Doug at the table, eating.

elements.speaker: JOHN
elements.text: You’re a very good police officer!
Doug pauses mid-bite, looks up from his food.

elements.speaker: TRUDY
elements.text: You know what really bugs me? That you never questioned Cheyenne.

elements.speaker: TRUDY
elements.text: About what? John, all of New Hampshire is out looking for Holly. Except her own mother. Doesn’t that strike you as a little odd?

elements.speaker: JOHN
elements.text: It’s over, Tru. The kid’s gone. Besides, I won’t be sticking around much longer. I’m going back to L.A.

elements.speaker: TRUDY
elements.text: Why do you hate this place so much?

elements.speaker: JOHN
elements.text: The real question is why do you pretend to love this place?
Pause. Trudy shakes her head in disgust.
She turns to go, but before she can get too far--

elements.speaker: JOHN
elements.text: What the fuck do you got against her, anyway?

elements.speaker: JOHN
elements.text: You never even tried to like her.

elements.speaker: TRUDY
elements.text: That is so not true! I never liked the way dad treated her.

elements.speaker: JOHN
elements.text: What the hell’s that supposed to mean?
John stands. Gets in Trudy’s face.

elements.speaker: JOHN
elements.text: You better watch what you say!

elements.speaker: TRUDY
elements.text: With a drug problem that dad always looked the other way on!

elements.speaker: TRUDY
elements.text: You know how many times she’s been arrested in the past two years?

elements.speaker: TRUDY
elements.text: Twelve! Never reprimanded. Never charged. Never even saw the inside of a jail cell. Maybe she would’ve been better off in there. Maybe

elements.speaker: JOHN
elements.text: Jesus. Why don’t you just say it?

elements.speaker: JOHN
elements.text: You were always jealous of Cheyenne and Holly, and how good dad treated them. Like they were his own.

elements.speaker: TRUDY
elements.text: Cheyenne never had to grow up, John... And neither did you.
John has no answer. He storms past Trudy and out of the room.
Denny’s. Through the diner window we see John sitting in a booth eating a late night breakfast, alone.
John at the cash, paying his bill. He says something to the hostess. She replies with a shrug and a shake of her head.

slugline: INT./EXT. JOHN’S CAR/STREETS OF DOVER - LATER
location_time: EXT. JOHN’S CAR/STREETS OF DOVER - LATER

elements.text: John drives through the slush-layered streets. From his recorded interview with Ricardo...

elements.speaker: RICARDO
elements.text: Two other men. Alberto Gomez and Raymond Olsen.

elements.speaker: JOHN
elements.text: Alberto and Raymond... Tell me more.

elements.speaker: RICARDO
elements.text: Raymond. He no longer works with us. They fired him... But I still see him sometimes, at the bar.

slugline: EXT. SILVER DOLLAR SALOON - LATE NIGHT

elements.text: Silver Dollar Saloon. Its marquee reads: Open Mic Nite.
John’s car pulls up and parks.

slugline: INT. SILVER DOLLAR SALOON - LATE NIGHT

elements.text: John enters to the sights and sounds of cowboys and cowgirls, lots of leather and American beer. Up on a small stage, a man in a cowboy get-up sings ‘Rhinestone Cowboy’.
John saddles up to the bar. Orders a beer from the bartender, then leans in to him...

elements.speaker: JOHN
elements.text: I’m supposed to meet a guy here. Name’s Raymond Olsen. See him around at all?

elements.speaker: BARTENDER
elements.text: Ray? Nah. Haven’t seen him since, jeez, a week ago?

elements.speaker: BARTENDER
elements.text: Strange. Guy never misses open mic.
Bartender produces from under the bar a small cardboard box containing about a dozen self-produced CD’s in their cases.

elements.speaker: BARTENDER
elements.text: He leaves these here. Take one if you want.
John lifts out a CD. A selfie of Raymond on the front cover-- hokey smile, decked out in a spiffy cowboy outfit with a guitar. He’s clearly mentally disabled. Though not profound.
Bartender walks off, leaving John with Raymond’s box of CD’s. John tries to pop open a case to look inside, but--
Cheyenne. She comes at him from behind and throws her arms around him. John pockets the CD case and half-turns and sees it’s her.
He pulls her off of him. She plops herself onto a bar stool. She’s still rolling on molly. John looks at her, contemptously.

elements.speaker: CHEYENNE
elements.text: Oh! I am so sorry, officer.
She keeps laughing. John suddenly yanks her off the barstool and practically drags her toward the exit.
Alleyway of the Silver Dollar. The side door bursts open and Cheyenne spills out, followed by John.

elements.speaker: CHEYENNE
elements.text: The fuck is your problem, man?
John keeps pulling her along down the alleyway.
POV: unseen driver, watching things escalate in the alley.

elements.speaker: JOHN
elements.text: Shut up. We’re just going to my car for a minute.
Cheyenne squirms, tries to run. John grabs her, pins her to the wall.

elements.speaker: JOHN
elements.text: No one else in town seems to be concerned with reeling you in. Now I wanna know why.

elements.speaker: JOHN
elements.text: Do you even give a shit that she’s gone?

elements.speaker: CHEYENNE
elements.text: She’s not gone. She’s coming back, and then everything will be fine. So leave me alone.
She breaks free, goes to flee. John yanks her back again.
The driver is the Hispanic and we’re in the Chrysler 300. He pops open his console and takes out his gun. He gets out of the car.
Cheyenne is practically pinned to the wall by John.

elements.speaker: JOHN
elements.text: Know how many of these cases I’ve worked? The chances of Holly just walking through your front door... Jesus, Chey, go play the Powerball if you want better odds.

elements.speaker: JOHN
elements.text: What was Mackie hiding? What was he up to?

elements.speaker: CHEYENNE
elements.text: Mackie was doing a helluva lot more than you are.

elements.speaker: JOHN
elements.text: I’m off the case. It’s the FBI’s now. Whatever you and Mackie were doing, they’re gonna find out.
Barrel of a gun touches John’s head. John freezes.

elements.speaker: CHEYENNE
elements.text: O’Shea. Baby. Don’t. He’s a friend.
O’SHEA roughs up John, shoves him up against the wall.

elements.speaker: CHEYENNE
elements.text: This is John. The guy I told you about.

elements.speaker: O’SHEA
elements.text: The cop from L.A.? Oh yeah? What’s your Cali ass doing snooping this far east?
In a flash, John disarms O’Shea of his weapon and has him on his knees about to snap his arm in half. Cheyenne screams.

elements.speaker: JOHN
elements.text: Everyone get the fuck in my car.
John in the driver’s seat. Cheyenne next to him. O’Shea sits in back, a bit emasculated.
John ejects the clip from O’Shea’s gun, empties the bullets into his hand, pockets them. He tosses the gun out the window into the snow.

elements.speaker: JOHN
elements.text: You can have it back when we’re finished.

elements.speaker: O’SHEA
elements.text: You best tell your friend he better watch his step.

elements.speaker: JOHN
elements.text: Hey, asshole. Her friend is still a member of law enforcement. And as such, her friend can still haul your worthless Cheech ass in for assault with a weapon on an off- duty police officer. Got that?

elements.speaker: CHEYENNE
elements.text: Why are you not working Holly’s case anymore?

elements.speaker: O’SHEA
elements.text: Cuz cops don’t give a fuck, that’s why.

elements.speaker: CHEYENNE
elements.text: You gotta stay on the case, John.

elements.speaker: CHEYENNE
elements.text: C’mon. You don’t understand, it’s like--

elements.speaker: JOHN
elements.text: You know what I don’t understand? Every time the music stops in this sick musical chairs, you two always seem to be the ones left standing? Now why is that?

elements.speaker: O’SHEA
elements.text: All I’m tryin’ to do is help her forget for a moment about this hell she’s in.

elements.speaker: O’SHEA
elements.text: Look, I know a lot of fucked up dudes who know a lotta fucked up dudes. If you know what I’m sayin’?

elements.speaker: O’SHEA
elements.text: Crickets. I ain’t proud to say it, but if this was some kinda heinous pedo underground shit, I would’ve heard about it by now.
Cheyenne gives O’Shea a pleading look. O’Shea softens, sighs--

elements.speaker: O’SHEA
elements.text: Except for that old Army cat.

elements.speaker: O’SHEA
elements.text: Straight-up local square. Been hittin me up every couple days. And for serious gear.

elements.speaker: O’SHEA
elements.text: They came to me. Yo, I had to give it up. Only way I was able to stay out of the equation.

elements.speaker: JOHN
elements.text: They were buying drugs? From you?

elements.speaker: O’SHEA
elements.text: Wasn’t no transaction. It was a mutha-fuckin’ salt and pepper shakedown. Every time. Pullin’ me over. Gangbustin’ my home and shit.

elements.speaker: O’SHEA
elements.text: More like what’d they rob. Like I said, crazy cocktail shit. High- grade. Pharmaceutical. Government. Military. You name it.

elements.speaker: O’SHEA
elements.text: When I told ‘em it’ll take a while, they got real pissed. Said they’re gonna pin Holly all on me.

elements.speaker: JOHN
elements.text: Are you sure about all this?

elements.speaker: O’SHEA
elements.text: Nah, we’re just all livin’ in the mutherfuckin’ Matrix. Of course I’m sure.

elements.speaker: O’SHEA
elements.text: I thought you were a cop. Didn’t you see Serpico? Sucka got shot in the face, yo! And I don’t wanna have to move to no Switzerland.
Cheyenne: It’s unclear whether she’s going to cry or be sick. Crying wins out.

elements.speaker: CHEYENNE
elements.text: I know I could’ve been a better mom. God, I know.

elements.speaker: CHEYENNE
elements.text: You gotta find her, John. I mean, this’ll be it for me. I’m going clean. NA, AA, fucking born again, whatever it takes...
John can’t meet her gaze. He opens the door, reaches into the snow and picks up the gun and hands it to O’Shea.
O’Shea takes the gun. He gets out and goes around to the front and helps Cheyenne out of the car.
Cheyenne gives John one more look, pleading, desperate, and then gets out and walks away, leaving John all alone. His thoughts race in all directions.
The night is very cold. John’s parked at the marina, looking out at the bay.
He turns the car on for some heat. He stuffs his hands into his coat pockets for extra warmth.
His hand feels something. He comes up with Raymond’s CD case.
He considers it a moment, tosses it onto the passenger seat.
He glances down to the case. He picks it up and opens it...
On the front of the disc, scrawled in black marker is the title of Raymond’s album: El Vaquero.
A revelation slams into John. El vaquero. He shoves his car into gear, mashes the gas pedal, and peels away.
The Rolling Stones, “Gimmie Shelter” begins to play over...
The mainland. A ferry laborer guides a line of waiting vehicles onto the ferry.
Mackie’s den. Decorating the walls are Mackie’s police commendations, awards, and military medals. Across the room stands a solid oak gun cabinet. It’s doors opened... A hunting rifle is missing...
Trudy in bed, wide awake. Doug fast asleep next to her. Trudy stares off at the window and the first light of dawn breaking through the curtains. The alarm clock goes off. Doug stirs.

The heavy metal door. Padlocked. “Gimmie Shelter”, now muffled, is clearly coming from somewhere in the cabin. On the workbench: used needles and a few empty vials. The locker is wide open. The bunny suit hanging there.
Raymond’s El Vaquero album still on the passenger seat. Next to it sits an open box of ammunition. Some shells missing.
The cabin. The property. John appears cutting across the snowy open field with his dad’s rifle in hand.

John reaches the cabin’s back door. He turns the doorknob. Locked. He fishes the keys out of his pocket, sticks the key in the lock. Key won’t turn. He tries again. Notta. He inspects the door knob and the deadbolt. Brand new. Locks have been changed. John steps back, raises a leg and boots the door in.
John enters. Takes in the mess -- dishes piled in the sink. Take-out containers and beer bottles litter the table.
“Gimmie Shelter” blasts from stereo speakers. The room itself in disarray. More beer cans and take-out boxes. Dirty laundry is strewn about, some of it spotted heavy with blood.
John appears, rifle at the ready. He sees the bloody clothes, yet he remains cop-calm. But behind the calm he’s amped.
He goes to the stereo and shuts off the music. He calls out:
His phone buzzes a text. He checks it.
From O’Shea: Army cat just took more gear.
John puts his phone away and starts checking the rest of the cabin. Room by room. Very tactical.
HALLWAY John moves down the hallway.
A MOAN is heard. Faint. Very eerie. Coming from somewhere in the cabin. John stops.
Another moan. Definitely a man’s. John listens. His gaze shifts to the floor beneath his feet. His focus turns to the end of the hallway and the cellar door.
The light snaps on and John comes down the stairs. Nobody here. He moves to the workbench, sees the vials, the needles. The bunny suit in the locker.
That moan again. Then a cry. John looks to the source: the door to the old furnace room. Padlocked.
John lays his rifle on the workbench, grabs a sledgehammer. He swings it into the padlock with a loud CLANK!
Reggie drives down the private cabin road, one hand on the wheel, the other holds a bit of cocaine in the crook of his thumb. He brings it up to his nose and snorts it.
He comes around a bend, sees John’s car parked just up ahead. He pulls in behind and idles.
He eyes John’s car. He shuts his truck off.
Reggie approaches, peeks in John’s front seat. Sees the box of ammunition. He glances down the road to the cabin.
He walks back to his truck, opens his door, and grabs his hunting rifle off the rack.
John swings the sledgehammer one more time, obliterating the lock off the door. He picks up his rifle, levels at the furnace door. With his free hand he yanks the door open...
Darkness. Next to him hangs a flashlight. He grabs it.
John silhouetted in the doorway. He flicks on the flashlight to reveal in the middle of the room...
John’s POV: A MAN IN A CHAIR. Black canvas bag over his head. Wrists bound to the chair.
John cautiously steps into the room. Rifle aimed at the man.
The man makes a guttural noise. He cries.
John steps over to the man. He has a work uniform on, laborers clothes -- blue collar shirt, blue pants.
Down the front of man’s shirt, from underneath the canvas bag, are dried-up rivulets of blood and pus and Lord knows what else.
John sweeps the flashlight down to the floor. The man is barefoot. Surrounding his feet is a stagnant puddle of urine and more blood.
John brings the light back up to the man, glimpsing a name stitched into the man’s work shirt. John steps closer, squints to read the name through all the crusted fluids...
The man stays silent. He begins to tremble. John finds the room’s light switch. He flicks it on.

elements.speaker: JOHN
elements.text: Alberto, it’s OK. I’m not going to hurt you. I’m going to take this bag off your head now, okay?
John pulls the bag off, revealing ALBERTO GOMEZ, blood-soaked face grotesque with a horror of sores and cuts. A rag has been stuffed into his mouth.
One eye is swollen shut. The other... well, there isn’t one -- as if scooped out with a melon baller.
John jerks back, almost stumbles. He lowers the rifle.
Alberto trembles with shock and terror. John removes the rag from Alberto’s mouth. Alberto’s lips quiver. He whispers...
Alberto’s expression returns to a vacant trauma, as John quickly digs out his cell phone, goes to dial 911.
From behind comes the sound of a Remington pump-action rifle. John freezes.

elements.speaker: REGGIE
elements.text: You’re way outta your jurisdiction, John.
John raises his hands. He slowly turns to face a coked-out Reggie brandishing his shotgun.
John tosses his phone. Reggie picks it up and pockets it.

elements.speaker: REGGIE
elements.text: Jesus Christ, just drop your gun.

elements.speaker: JOHN
elements.text: El Vaquero is a man named Raymond Olsen. You got the wrong guy.

elements.speaker: REGGIE
elements.text: This scumbag beaner. He raped Holly. He already confessed.

elements.speaker: JOHN
elements.text: Was that before you gouged his eye out or after?

elements.speaker: REGGIE
elements.text: I’m givin’ you a chance here, Johnny.

elements.speaker: REGGIE
elements.text: Drop the fucking gun, go on back to L.A., and let me handle this.
John doesn’t comply. He begins to slowly raise his rifle.

elements.speaker: REGGIE
elements.text: You dumb motherfucker. Drop that fucking gun!
John, rifle fully levelled at Reggie.

elements.speaker: JOHN
elements.text: You got the wrong guy. This isn’t El Vaquero. This isn’t right.

elements.speaker: REGGIE
elements.text: You’re forcing my hand here, John!

elements.speaker: JOHN
elements.text: This is my property. I want you to turn around and leave. Or I’ll be forced to defend myself.

elements.speaker: REGGIE
elements.text: Your father was my buddy. My man! In his last moments, we were together... me and him... in the goddamn fucking ambulance!

elements.speaker: REGGIE
elements.text: I made him a promise: that I’d finish what we started. This is our town.

elements.speaker: REGGIE
elements.text: Fuck that! What do you know about what’s right?! Your father not turning you in 20 years ago? Was that right? You’re goddamn right it was! Now stand down, soldier!

elements.speaker: REGGIE
elements.text: I ain’t breakin’ my promise! May the Lord be my witness, you’ve made your choice, Detective.
Reggie takes aim at John’s head.
Reggie pulls the trigger. John kicks the heavy furnace room door closed, shielding the Remington’s spray of buckshot.
The gun blast is EAR-SPLITTING. Alberto screams. John stays composed. He pops out of the room and returns fire--
A howl from Reggie. John ducks back into the room, glances to Alberto -- in his tortured state it’s tough to tell if he’s been hit.
A commotion upstairs, things falling, breaking. A door being thrown open. Then nothing but Alberto’s wails.
John turns and races out of the room after Reggie.
Leading with his gun, John comes out of the cellar. Blood trails the hallway. John follows it.
Blood smears the back door that’s barely being held together by its hinges. John steps out and onto the patio, pauses.
Ahead of him the blood trail thickens, stretching across the snowy property and into the forest.
John in the woods. He climbs up a small hill. Crests it. On the other side he sees:
Reggie. Sitting propped against a tree, head leaned back, clutching his rifle on his lap. His chest and shoulder perforated by John’s buckshot.
As John approaches, rifle aimed squarely at Reggie--

elements.speaker: REGGIE
elements.text: Mackie looked after that little girl... like she was his own...
Reggie tosses the rifle off to his side. He winces in pain. He struggles for air. Lungs collapsing from buckshot.
Holly to church? Not once. No first communion. No confession. Never even baptized. Believe that?
He coughs blood. Wipes his mouth of it. His face greys. He’s fading fast.

elements.speaker: REGGIE
elements.text: Nah... You know what happens if you don’t get baptized? Devil finds you. You stick out like a sore thumb. Mackie wanted to change that. Started takin’ Holly to Sunday service. Him and Trudy...
An odd peace falls over Reggie. He shuts his eyes.
gotta have God on your team...
He opens his eyes, looks up at John standing over him. He takes one last breath, and then he’s gone.
John stands there, looking down at Reggie as a light snow begins to fall over the forest.
A phone rings... In Reggie’s pocket. John’s ringtone. John cautiously goes for the phone, takes it out, never taking his eyes or gun off Reggie.
John’s POV: his cell. Caller ID: Doug. John answers.

elements.speaker: DOUG
elements.text: John. They they found Holly’s body.

elements.speaker: DOUG
elements.text: Washed up on the bay this morning.
John sinks. Every fiber of his being sinks. He looks over at the lifeless Reggie.

elements.speaker: DOUG
elements.text: I’m sorry, John. We really tried.
An air ambulance helicopter roars in over the treetops, emerging onto the open field of the cabin property. Its rotor wash kicks up a blizzard of snow.
John stands at the edge of the property, numbly smoking a cigarette and watching Reggie being carried by EMS out of the forest in a bodybag.
Alberto, on mobile life support, is quickly lifted into the air ambulance.
John is questioned by officers, who write down his every word. They shake hands. John tosses his cigarette away. He turns and walks off toward the road.
John’s car pulls up outside the townhouse. Followed by a Dover PD cruiser. John climbs out of his car and heads toward Cheyenne’s front door.
Doug gets out of his cruiser but stays behind, watching.

Cheyenne opens her door. She sees John. She instantly knows. An unspoken moment between them. John struggles, then breaks the news. A moment... Cheyenne collapses. John catches her before the fall, into his arms. He remains stoic. She is in hysterics. PASSAGE OF TIME SEQUENCE...

slugline: INT. KIERSTEAD HOME - JOHN’S BEDROOM - NIGHT

elements.text: John sits in a chair, heavy mood. Beer in one hand, a baseball in the other. Several empty beer cans clutter the window sill. He absently cycles through pitch grips.

Holly’s wake. A small framed portrait of Holly stands on an equally small casket. The room is jam-packed. John is here. As is Doug, Captain Marchand, and many others. Cheyenne is up front in a black dress next to a glum O’Shea in a dark suit. Cheyenne is lost, part of her has died, and without anymore tears to shed for it.
Alberto Gomez, comatose in a hospital bed, hooked up to a crowd of wires, tubes, and ventilators.
A bright, sterile room. The preparation room. Alone on a metal table sits a bronze urn, engraved with:
As Holly’s mourners file out of the viewing room, Captain Marchand approaches John.

elements.speaker: CAPTAIN MARCHAND
elements.text: Three funerals in two weeks. How are you holding up?

elements.speaker: JOHN
elements.text: I shouldn’t complain, considering with the ground frozen, Cheyenne has to wait five long months just to bury her daughter.

elements.speaker: CAPTAIN MARCHAND
elements.text: Amazingly enough, looks like he’ll pull through. Of course, he’ll be extradited back to Mexico.
The two men exit the parlor.

elements.speaker: CAPTAIN MARCHAND
elements.text: Turns out Reginald Lund was right.

elements.speaker: CAPTAIN MARCHAND
elements.text: Gomez was a registered sex offender. Multiple rapes of minors back in Mexico City. Escaped custody six months ago. I guess he fled as far north as he could get.

elements.speaker: JOHN
elements.text: So Reggie got his El Vaquero.
John and the Captain look out at the mourners returning to their cars. Cheyenne is led to the Chrysler 300 by O’Shea.

elements.speaker: CAPTAIN MARCHAND
elements.text: It’s still an open case. Bureau is investigating. As are we.
John watches Cheyenne in the 300’s passenger seat. She looks out the window at John.

elements.speaker: CAPTAIN MARCHAND
elements.text: But with no known fixed address, we just haven’t had any promising leads, aside from occasional sightings at homeless shelters, churches. But we’ll find him.
The 300 pulls away. John watches it until it disappears.

elements.speaker: CAPTAIN MARCHAND
elements.text: Look, despite our obvious differences in methodology, I want to thank you for everything that you’ve done.
Captain places his hand onto John’s shoulder, reassuringly.

elements.speaker: CAPTAIN MARCHAND
elements.text: Your father would be very proud of
John nods. Looks away. Knowing he’ll keep the truth of his father’s involvement forever a secret.
The Captain and John part ways.
Low-income housing. The rings go on, until--

elements.speaker: DISPATCH
elements.text: Good morning, Dover Police Department, how may we help you?

slugline: INT. LOW INCOME UNIT - BATHROOM - MORNING

elements.text: RAYMOND OLSEN (mid-40’s) in front of his bathroom mirror. Fresh from the shower, towel at his waist. He meticulously combs his hair. Clearly, he has Down Syndrome.
His voice comes in, harboring a speech deficit -- his words stuttering and slow to form...

elements.speaker: RAYMOND
elements.text: I would like to speak to Federal agents in charge of the Holly Roberts investigation.
He puts down his comb. He studies his reflection.
Trudy in her bedroom, kneeling bed-side, a rosary wrapped around her hands as she recites the Hail Mary...

elements.speaker: TRUDY
elements.text: Hail Mary, full of grace, the Lord is with thee...

slugline: INT. LOW INCOME UNIT - BATHROOM - MORNING

elements.text: BEDROOM Raymond dresses himself. Conservative church wear. Dockers, loafers, a white button-up dress shirt.

elements.speaker: TRUDY
elements.text: Blessed are thou among women, and blessed is the fruit of thy womb, Jesus...
A neatly kept kitchen. Raymond at the table eating a breakfast of grapefruit and coffee.

elements.speaker: TRUDY
elements.text: Holy Mary, mother of God, pray for our sinners, now and at the hour of our death. Amen.
Raymond walks into his small, empty living room, over to a far wall where he has built a makeshift SHRINE:
Two large paintings hung side by side on the wall. One is of Jesus. The other, a grotesque rendition of Lucifer.
Beneath these paintings hangs a small portrait of Holly.
Xmas lights have been strung around the shrine. Raymond plugs them in. The lights come on, flashing multi-colors.
Raymond kneels before the shrine. He makes the sign of the cross, clasps his hands in prayer, and begins to recite...

elements.speaker: RAYMOND
elements.text: Hail Mary, full of grace, the Lord is with thee...

elements.speaker: TRUDY
elements.text: Blessed are thou among women, and blessed is the fruit of thy womb, Jesus...
Raymond with his eyes closed. His words matching Trudy’s--

elements.speaker: RAYMOND/TRUDY
elements.text: Holy Mary, mother of God, pray for our sinners, now and at the hour of our death. Amen.

elements.speaker: RAYMOND/TRUDY
elements.text: Hail Mary, full of grace, the Lord is with thee...
Front lawn of the apartment building. Creeping into frame from behind us is a single file of about a dozen heavily- armed men donning FBI jackets.

elements.speaker: RAYMOND/TRUDY
elements.text: Blessed are thou among women, and blessed is the fruit of thy womb, Jesus...

slugline: INT. LOW INCOME HOUSING - HALLWAY - MORNING

elements.text: The Federal agents enter the hallway, swiftly yet cautiously. They step up to unit 204. Flank the door. Guns at the ready.

elements.speaker: RAYMOND/TRUDY
elements.text: Holy Mary, mother of God, pray for our sinners...
Lead agent nods to another agent who hoists a battering ram. The other agents step back. Everyone poised. Totally juiced.

elements.speaker: RAYMOND/TRUDY
elements.text: ... now and at the hour of our death...
The battering ram winds up, and....
BOOM! Raymond’s front door splinters and drops. The agents storm into the unit.
Agents descend onto Raymond, who doesn’t even budge. He was expecting this. Feds shout orders at Raymond. “Hands up!” “Get down!” “On the floor!”.
Raymond is slammed to the floor, face first. He’s handcuffed. Amid the chaos, he repeats the final word of prayer...
John at an airport bar with his carry-on and a one-way ticket back to L.A. He sips his drink. The TV above the bar grabs his attention. Breaking newscast --

elements.speaker: ANCHOR WOMAN
elements.text: Breaking news out of Dover this morning: A major break in the case of Holly Roberts, the missing Dover girl whose body was discovered last week washed ashore along the Piscataqua River....
Anchor woman at her desk, the graphic at her shoulder is a picture of smiling Holly next to a mugshot of Raymond.

elements.speaker: ANCHOR WOMAN
elements.text: ...FBI officials have now confirmed evidence from Internet chat rooms and cell phone records, connecting local man, Raymond Olsen, to the kidnapping and murder of Holly. Mr. Olsen is currently in Federal custody and is awaiting trial pending a psychological evaluation. He has pleaded not guilty.
John sets down his drink. Slight relief washes over him. His phone rings. It’s Doug. John answers.

elements.speaker: JOHN
elements.text: Doug. I just heard. Ya got him.

elements.speaker: DOUG
elements.text: Uh... Do you, uh... Have you seen Trudy?
John bursts through the precinct doors and past the front desk officer.
An upset Doug paces outside Interview Room Two. John enters the hallway. Doug sees John.

elements.speaker: DOUG
elements.text: He just started spewing all this shit about Trudy. Why would he say that, John?

elements.speaker: DOUG
elements.text: Why would he say those things?

elements.speaker: JOHN
elements.text: I don’t know. But just -- we’ll figure it out. OK? Get outta here for a while. Go take a break.
John enters the Interview Room. Doug lingers a beat, hesitates, then leaves.
Captain Marchand watches through a two-way mirror. On the other side, Federal Agents grill a frightened Raymond. John enters the observation room. Captain looks to him.

elements.speaker: CAPTAIN MARCHAND
elements.text: I dunno where he’s getting this stuff, but he seems convinced.
John looks in at Raymond and the Feds.
Raymond sits with a mixed expression of fear and annoyance. A FEDERAL AGENT looms over him.

elements.speaker: FEDERAL AGENT
elements.text: You’re not being honest with us, Raymond. Time to man-up, dude.

elements.speaker: RAYMOND
elements.text: It’s OK. She said it’s OK. She said I would be doing the Lord’s work. I don’t wanna make Him angry. No. It was OK. I was doing the Lord’s work.

elements.speaker: FEDERAL AGENT
elements.text: Yeah, we know Trudy was helping you, Raymond. But you’re not answering the fucking question: Why did you kill Holly? Why did you do it, Raymond?

elements.speaker: RAYMOND
elements.text: No! I was doing the Lord’s work!

elements.speaker: FEDERAL AGENT
elements.text: Fuck that. You came to Trudy for help. You came to the church for help. You lost your job. You fucked up and now you got zero prospects. Shit, man, you got no money. Barely a home. Tell me...

elements.speaker: FEDERAL AGENT
elements.text: Who’s gonna wanna hire a retard?

elements.speaker: FEDERAL AGENT
elements.text: You sought counsel. But it wasn’t enough. And when you felt that God turned his back on you, you went off. Didn’t you? You got revenge.

elements.speaker: RAYMOND
elements.text: No. What? No... I gave her back. I gave Holly back to Trudy. Everything was OK.

elements.speaker: FEDERAL AGENT
elements.text: Fuck you, you gave her back. You drowned her in the Bay. How many times we gotta go over that?

elements.speaker: FEDERAL AGENT
elements.text: What happened before you killed her?

elements.speaker: FEDERAL AGENT
elements.text: She mocked you, didn’t she? Didn’t wanna kiss the retard. Get retard cooties. Yuck! Bleh!

elements.speaker: RAYMOND
elements.text: I wanna go home now. I wanna play my guitar.

elements.speaker: FEDERAL AGENT
elements.text: You can’t go home, Raymond. I’m afraid home no longer exists for you. Time to play a different tune. How ‘bout twenty five to life? You know that one?
John and Captain stare in at Raymond.

elements.speaker: CAPTAIN MARCHAND
elements.text: I’m gonna assume you know nothing about any of this.

elements.speaker: CAPTAIN MARCHAND
elements.text: Do you believe that what he claims holds any validity?
John is quiet, struggles genuinely for an answer.
Suddenly, a man in a suit enters the Interrogation Room, followed by a woman.
The man gets in between Raymond and the Federal Agent.

elements.speaker: MAN
elements.text: This is Dr. Shephard, his psychiatrist.
Raymond begins to cry. Dr. Shephard goes to him.

elements.speaker: LAWYER
elements.text: My client has not been evaluated. Everything he just told you is inadmissable.
Raymond, more upset, beings to wail. Dr. Shephard tries to calm him. Raymond pushes Dr. Shephard away.

elements.speaker: LAWYER
elements.text: You’re monsters. Really. Monsters. You know that?
Raymond starts to thrash his head against the metal tabletop. Over and over. Blood comes out.
John’s had enough. He goes to leave. Captain stops him.

elements.speaker: CAPTAIN MARCHAND
elements.text: All due respect, John, just so we’re clear: you had your shot at this. Let us handle Trudy.

elements.speaker: JOHN
elements.text: I’m sure you got your best men on it.
John walks briskly down the hallway. A rattled Doug approaches with coffee.
John driving Dover, seemingly without aim. He turns a corner and is suddenly cut off by police barricades and a cop car blocking the road, lights flashing.
John slows. Stops. Up ahead coming into view is... A PARADE. The Dover Annual Santa Claus Parade. John takes a detour down a side road.
The parade. Children, parents, the elderly in lawn chairs bundled up in blankets with their hot cocoa. Everyone a kid again. Anxious to glimpse the man himself, Santa.

Front steps of a church with a view of the street. John’s car drives past and out of sight. A squeal of car brakes. John’s car reverses fast back into view and screeches to a halt. See now what he sees -- Trudy’s car. Tucked away in a corner of the church parking lot.

John enters the church. Looks around. Just a couple nuns up front lighting candles. They leave. No sign of Trudy. John dips his fingers into the holy water stoup, makes the sign of the cross. He starts down the aisle. Somewhere the click of a door opening. John looks across to see a priest exiting a confessional booth. The priest sees John. The two share a look. The priest walks off.
John approaches the booth. He opens it and slips inside.

John sits in the priest’s chair. A screen of lattice work separates him from the person kneeling on the other side. It’s Trudy. She looks to John, barely able to make eye contact. Through the screen John can see that she’s nervous as hell. John looks about. He smiles.

elements.speaker: JOHN
elements.text: Little creepy sitting on this side.

elements.speaker: JOHN
elements.text: How many times as a kid I sat where you’re sitting? In this same booth.
Trudy, all bottled up, remains a million miles away.

elements.speaker: JOHN
elements.text: Remember the bullshit we used to spew in here? Not doing homework. Saying curse words. Lying to mom and dad.

elements.speaker: JOHN
elements.text: But the biggest sins were always the ones we were too afraid to admit.

elements.speaker: TRUDY
elements.text: John. Have you ever criticized God?
John stays quiet, unsure what to say. Trudy confesses--

elements.speaker: TRUDY
elements.text: I did. Twice. When mom died I had my first doubts.

elements.speaker: TRUDY
elements.text: And when I found out I couldn’t have children--

elements.speaker: JOHN
elements.text: I never should’ve gotten into that boat.

elements.speaker: JOHN
elements.text: Dad was supposed to take me to a pitching clinic down in Boston. I said I wanted to hang out with my friends instead.

elements.speaker: JOHN
elements.text: He was just trying to do what he thought was right, but still... I killed my best friend, Tru. And I never had to answer for it.
A stunned Trudy. John watches her a moment. She seems torn.

elements.speaker: JOHN
elements.text: Whatever happened we can figure it
She looks to John, sees a knowledge in him.

elements.speaker: JOHN
elements.text: He knows Dad and Reggie took matters into their own hands, but that they got the wrong guy.

elements.speaker: JOHN
elements.text: Just tell me you’re not responsible for Holly’s murder. Tell me a 45 year-old with Down Syndrome has it all wrong.
Trudy trembles. John slides the screen back. He takes her hands in his.

elements.speaker: JOHN
elements.text: Look at me. Look at me, Tru.

elements.speaker: JOHN
elements.text: It might not hurt much right now. You might think you can get away with this. But wait twenty years, and you’ll regret the day you walked into your own hell.
Trudy turns her head, wipes away a tear.
Trudy, tears running, emotions bottle-necked, utters quietly:
Something in John had hoped she’d say “no”. He slowly let’s go of her.

elements.speaker: TRUDY
elements.text: I hired Raymond to take her. It was just for a few days.

elements.speaker: TRUDY
elements.text: I wanted to teach Cheyenne a lesson. I wanted to show her how much she had to lose. Show her what it means not to have children. Then we’d let Holly go.

slugline: EXT. THE BAY - SMALL BOAT - DAY

elements.text: Way out on the bay in a small boat. The Dover coast in the distance. Trudy’s at the helm.

elements.speaker: TRUDY
elements.text: When Dad got involved... I didn’t know what to do. I was scared. I knew it wouldn’t take long before they got to Raymond. I panicked.
Holly is on the boat. Hands bound. Blindfolded. She is clothed in crisp, white garments. She trembles.

elements.speaker: TRUDY
elements.text: So I got her back from Raymond.
The boat enters a thick fog bank. Trudy cuts the engine.

elements.speaker: TRUDY
elements.text: She was interested in the Church, in Jesus. Dad and I took her to Sunday school every week. I taught her the Bible. She took First Communion, and then Confirmation.
Cheyenne wasn’t happy about it. But Holly was excited. She was almost there. I was her Godmother.
Trudy holds a copy of the Bible in her hand. She leads a terrified Holly over to the edge of the boat.

elements.speaker: TRUDY
elements.text: All that was left was the baptism.
Holly struggles. Trudy forces Holly’s head overboard.
As Holly’s head is thrust down into the frigid waters of the bay. Held there. She writhes and struggles mightily.
Trudy hauls Holly up. Holly cries as Trudy recites--

elements.speaker: TRUDY
elements.text: Praise to you, almighty God and Father, for you have created water to cleanse and to give new life.
She dunks Holly again. Holds her under. Holly flails.

elements.speaker: TRUDY
elements.text: Father, look now with love upon your Church, and unseal for her the fountain of baptism...
Holly is lifted up again. She screams for help.

elements.speaker: TRUDY
elements.text: ... so that all who have been buried with Christ by Baptism into death may rise again to life with Him, in the unity of the Holy Spirit, one God, for ever and ever. Amen.
Holly is forced back under. Close on Trudy’s face, full of fervor, as she recites her vows--

elements.speaker: TRUDY
elements.text: Do you reject Satan and all his works and all his empty promises?

elements.speaker: TRUDY
elements.text: Do you believe in God, the Father almighty, creator of heaven and earth?

elements.speaker: TRUDY
elements.text: I do... Do you believe in Jesus Christ, his only Son, our Lord? And do you believe in the Holy Spirit--
Holly begins to overpower Trudy. Trudy strikes Holly across her head. Repeatedly. She shoves her head deeper underwater.
TRUDY (CONT’D)  the -- the holy Catholic Church,     life communion of saints, the forgiveness of sins, the resurrection of the body, and everlasting?
Trudy feels the resistance leave Holly. She let’s go of her, watches her, half overboard, bobbing lifelessly.
Trudy’s expression matches the horror she felt on the boat.

elements.speaker: TRUDY
elements.text: I don’t remember much after that. Maybe I held her under for too long. Maybe I hit her harder than I thought I did. I -- I don’t know.
John watches her. A long moment passes. Finally--
Trudy looks up at John, wipes tears from her eyes.
John digs into his pocket. He comes up with the keys to his rental car. He holds them out to Trudy.

elements.speaker: JOHN
elements.text: Soon all of New England’s gonna be out looking for you. At least this way you get a chance to think.
Trudy realizes. She takes out her car keys. Her and John make the exchange.

elements.speaker: JOHN
elements.text: Rental’s due back at the airport in the morning.

elements.speaker: TRUDY
elements.text: What are you going to tell people?

elements.speaker: JOHN
elements.text: Nothing. It’s between you and God now.
John reaches in through the open partition. He kisses Trudy on the forehead. She holds him. He pulls away, looks at her--
John approaches Trudy’s car. He unlocks it and climbs in. He starts it up and drives away.
John stops at an intersection as the final leg of the Santa Claus parade rolls by.
A parade float passes carrying Santa’s Workshop: elves making toys and the big man himself, Santa, sitting atop his sleigh. He waves at the parade-goers. He waves at John.
John’s POV: Holly’s two friends, Beth and Krista, are aboard the Santa float, dressed as elves and holding their hobbyhorses.
John watches them, their expressions -- the illusion of safety and innocence ripped from them forever.
John pulls into the driveway of a well-kept bungalow.
John, car idling, stares out at the home. He shuts off the car and climbs out.

slugline: INT. ANDY’S PARENTS HOME - MOMENTS LATER

elements.text: A doorbell chimes. A woman appears (60’s). She opens the door to see John standing here on the stoop.
MRS. MURPHY pauses. Her eyes narrow at John. Then it clicks--
MR. MURPHY appears behind his wife. These are Andy’s parents. John stays on the stoop, looking hesitant.
The Murphy’s look John in the eyes, trying to read him.

elements.speaker: MR. MURPHY
elements.text: Would you like to come inside, John?

elements.speaker: JOHN
elements.text: There’s something I have to tell you.
